AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: To evaluate the impact of obesity and morbid obesity on short-term outcomes after laparoscopic adrenalectomy.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: The study included 520 consecutive patients undergoing laparoscopic adrenalectomy for adrenal tumor. The entire study group was divided depending on the body mass index: group 1 (normal weight), <25 kg/m(2) ; group 2 (overweight), 25-30 kg/m(2) ; and group 3 (obese) 30-40 kg/m(2) . Additionally, group 4 (morbidly obese) was distinguished. Study end-points were: operative time, intraoperative blood loss, total length of hospital stay, morbidity rate and 30-day readmission rate.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The mean operative times were 88.8, 94.7, 93.5, and 99.9 min in groups 1, 2, 3 and 4, respectively (P = 0.1444). Complications were comparable between groups (12.8% vs 8.8% vs 8.2% vs 11.5%, P = 0.5295). The mean intraoperative blood loss was 66.8 versus 78.3 versus 60.7 versus 92.4, P = 0.1399. There were no differences in conversion rate between groups.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Obesity has no influence on short-term outcomes of laparoscopic transperitoneal adrenalectomy. This procedure is feasible regardless of the body mass index. Therefore, it can be offered to all patient groups including those morbidly obese individuals in whose case preoperative weight loss seems unnecessary.
